normalized.why: Trimmed and upper-cased before anything else looks at it. A Mac's disk is case-insensitive but case-preserving, so ICS3U and ics3u cannot both exist as folders — settling the case here is what stops a clash check missing one.

courseCode.note: What a course code may be. ONE rule, asked by the New Course wizard and by renaming a course, because a code one accepts and the other refuses is a course a teacher can create and then never re-type. The rule is narrow because a course code is not just a label: it IS the folder name under courses/, it is written into course_config.json for the shared Python, it prefixes every backup and archive zip, and on the mac it becomes part of a scheduled publish's launchd label. Each of those has its own opinion about what it will carry; one narrow rule beats four that disagree at the edges.

problems.why: An empty field is not-ready-yet, not an error. A warning that appears before the teacher has typed anything is noise.

problems.expectProblem: A course code cannot contain spaces.
problems.why: Checked before the general character rule so the commonest mistake gets the sentence that names it.

problems.expectProblem: A course named ICS4U already exists — choose a different code.
problems.why: The clash is found case-insensitively — see normalized.

problems.expectProblem: A course named MPM2D already exists — choose a different code.
A course code can only use letters and numbers.
A course code can only use letters and numbers.
problems.why: A hyphen is refused like any other punctuation. Clubs are named by the teacher, so this is the rule most likely to meet one — it is narrow on purpose, and CSCLUB is available.

problems.expectProblem: A course code can only use letters and numbers.
problems.why: Emoji fail the same test punctuation does: not an ASCII letter or digit.

problems.expectProblem: A course code can only use letters and numbers.
problems.why: An accented letter is refused too. The sentence says letters and numbers, which is true of what is ALLOWED — the alternative is a sentence about character encodings in a sidebar row.
Eight characters. Ontario codes are six; clubs are named by the teacher, and eight leaves room for this one without letting a code grow into a sentence.

problems.expectProblem: A course code can be at most 8 characters.

problems.why: A course does not clash with itself. Re-typing a course's own code while renaming it is a teacher changing their mind, which is allowed.
Nor does it clash with its own capitalisation.

problems.expectProblem: A course named MPM2D already exists — choose a different code.
problems.why: Renaming onto ANOTHER course's code is still a clash.

renameEffects.why: The code IS the folder name under courses/, so renaming is a move. Everything inside the folder travels with it untouched.

The app reads a course's code from its FOLDER name while the site builder and the social-card maker read it from course_config.json. A pair that disagree produce a sidebar saying one thing and a published page saying another, with no error anywhere.
course_name is the teacher's own wording and is editable in Course Settings. Rewriting a title they may have hand-written, because they changed a code, is the kind of helpfulness that loses work.

They stay in courses/_backups/<OLD CODE>/ under the names they were made with, because that is what they are: a copy of the course as it stood, when it was called that. Restoring one still works — the restorer names the restored folder after the ITEM rather than after whatever the zip holds inside.

Where a section publishes to is recorded INSIDE the course folder (.netlify_sites/section<N>.json), so it moves with it and the site's address does not change. A rename is a change to the teacher's filing, not a move of their students' URL.

The one thing renaming has to break. A scheduled publish is an alarm held OUTSIDE the working folder, addressed by the old code, and after a rename it would fire at a course that is no longer there. It is turned off and the teacher is told — silently losing a scheduled publish is the failure worth spending an alert on.

cases.why: No digit in the fourth place, so no grade is claimed.
Too short to have a fourth character.
A digit that is not 1–4 is honest about not knowing rather than silently dropping it.

gradeLabels.note: The grade named by an Ontario course code's FOURTH character, matching the wizard. A club code with no digit there gets no grade label at all rather than a wrong one.

note: Names on disk and the rules for adding a section. All of it is string handling over files both apps read, so all of it ports — and the naming grammar in particular MUST, because the two apps list each other's files. A course backed up on a Mac and opened on Windows has to appear in the Backups list, not vanish because the parser was rewritten from memory.

entryProblems.why: An empty field is quietly invalid: nothing has been said yet, so there is nothing to warn about. A warning that appears before the teacher types is noise.

entryProblems.expectProblem: “0” isn’t a section number — sections are 1 or higher.
“-2” isn’t a section number — sections are 1 or higher.
“two” isn’t a section number — sections are 1 or higher.

sectionNumbers.note: Adding a section: what is offered, what is refused, and in whose words.

suggested.why: The SMALLEST number not in use, not one past the highest — so 'add section 1' and 'add the next one' are each a single click.

timestampFormat.note: The `created:` frontmatter stamp the wizard writes, matched exactly so pages added later sit beside pages made at setup without a teacher seeing two forms.

cases.name: ICS3U_backup_2026-08-11_221530_assistant-section3.zip
cases.why: The assistant's own backups say so in the name, so a teacher can see which copies Plantoir made and what each was for. A name WITHOUT that ending is one of the teacher's own — which is exactly what every backup made before this existed is, and why the suffix is added rather than the teacher's being marked.

cases.name: 2026-08-10_143005.zip
cases.why: The setup wizard's automatic zip. It belongs to neither list.

cases.name: ICS3U_backup_2026-08-11_221530_something-else.zip
cases.why: An unrecognised maker makes the WHOLE name unrecognised, rather than quietly reading as a teacher's own backup. A backup attributed to the wrong maker is worse than one not listed.

cases.name: MCV4U_backup_2026-08-11_221530.zip
cases.why: Another course's backup, when reading ICS3U's folder.

zipNames.note: Three kinds of zip live side by side in `courses/_backups/<CODE>/`, told apart by NAME. Each parser accepts only its own form, so the three can never appear in each other's lists — an archive showing up under Backups is a teacher restoring the wrong thing. The timestamp is `yyyy-MM-dd_HHmmss` and contains an underscore of its own, which is why the pieces are counted rather than split on the last underscore.
